Looking at the test image, I see a corn ear with:
- Healthy yellow kernels on the left side
- Olive-green to gray-green mold covering kernels on the right side
- Powdery/dusty appearance to the fungal growth
- Infection appearing on ear surface

This suggests an ear rot disease. Let me view reference images for the ear rot candidates and other diseases.

Perfect! I can see the ear rot patterns clearly now. Let me compare:

- **Aspergillus**: Olive-green to gray-green dusty mold - this matches the test image very well
- **Trichoderma**: Dark green mold, noticeably darker than the test image
- **Diplodia**: White mycelium - not matching at all
- **Fusarium**: White to pink/salmon - not matching

The test image shows olive-green/gray-green mold that matches Aspergillus. Let me view two more references to be thorough:

Excellent! Now I have viewed 6 reference images. Let me analyze:

**Comparison Summary:**

1. **Ear_rots_Gibberella** - Shows pink/reddish mold, not matching the green-gray color
2. **Gray_leaf_spot** - Shows leaf lesions, not ear/kernel disease

**The test image clearly shows:**
- Olive-green to gray-green powdery mold on corn kernels
- Partial coverage of the ear
- Dusty/powdery texture
- Characteristic color that matches Aspergillus perfectly

**Why not other ear rots:**
- NOT Trichoderma: Too dark green (Trichoderma is much darker)
- NOT Diplodia: White mycelium, not green
- NOT Fusarium: White to pink/salmon, not green
- NOT Gibberella: Pink/red mold, not green
- NOT Gray_leaf_spot: Affects leaves, not ear kernels

The olive-green to gray-green dusty mold on the kernel surface is the diagnostic signature of **Aspergillus ear rot**. This matches the knowledge base description perfectly: "Olive-green to gray-green powdery mold on corn kernels" with spores that appear dusty.
